chunks: From him, from Faḍālah, from Abān, from Abī Maryam, from Abī Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said:
The injuries of women are at half of the injuries of men in everything.

key_terms.الرِّجَالِ: men, whose injuries serve as the comparative legal measure
key_terms.النِّسَاءِ: women, as the legal subject discussed in the ruling
key_terms.النِّصْفِ: one half, indicating the proportion set in the ruling
key_terms.جِرَاحَاتُ: bodily injuries or wounds subject to legal assessment
key_terms.جِرَاحَاتِ: injuries, referring here to compensable bodily harm
key_terms.فِي كُلِّ شَيْءٍ: in everything, indicating general applicability within the scope of the ruling

ai.seo_question: What does Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām say about the legal assessment of women’s injuries compared to men’s injuries?
ai.summary: This hadith states a legal ruling concerning compensation or assessment of bodily injuries, establishing that the injuries of women are reckoned at half of those of men in all cases. It appears in a chapter dealing with retaliatory law and legal parity between different categories of persons.
